title: Python Todo CLI
description:
Build a minimal command-line todo manager in Python.

## Goals
- Users can add, list, and complete todo items from the command line
- Persistent storage via JSON file
- No external dependencies

## Success Criteria
- User can add a new todo item
- User can list all todos
- User can mark a todo as complete
- Todos persist across runs

## Out of Scope for MVP
- Due dates or priorities
- SQLite storage
- Multiple lists
- Color output

title: User can manage todos via CLI
description:
Users can perform basic todo management from the command line.

## User Stories
- As a user, I can add a todo so I can track what I need to do
- As a user, I can list todos so I can see what's pending
- As a user, I can mark a todo as complete so I can track progress

## Acceptance Criteria
- [ ] `python3 todo.py add "text"` creates a new todo
- [ ] `python3 todo.py list` shows all todos with IDs and status
- [ ] `python3 todo.py complete <id>` marks a todo as done
- [ ] Completed todos show a visual indicator
- [ ] Data persists in todos.json across runs

## Technical Notes
- Single file app with TodoApp class
- argparse for CLI
- JSON file persistence
- unittest for tests

title: Implement add and list commands
description:
Implement the ability to add and list todo items.

## Requirements
- TodoApp class in todo.py with add() and list_todos() methods
- `python3 todo.py add "Buy groceries"` creates a todo
- `python3 todo.py list` prints all todos with ID prefix and text
- Each todo: {id, text, completed, created_at}
- IDs: first 8 chars of uuid4
- Persistence: load/save todos.json
- Empty input rejected with error message

## Implementation Notes
- Use argparse with subcommands
- TodoApp.__init__ loads from JSON file, creates empty list if missing
- save() writes to todos.json after each mutation
- list output format: `[id] text` or `[id] [done] text`

## Test Specifications

### Unit Tests (test_todo.py)
- test_add_todo_creates_item_with_correct_fields
- test_add_todo_rejects_empty_text
- test_list_todos_returns_all_items
- test_persistence_survives_reload

### Manual Verification
- python3 todo.py add "Test item" → prints confirmation
- python3 todo.py list → shows the item
- Restart and list again → item still there

title: Implement complete command
description:
Implement the ability to mark todo items as complete.

## Requirements
- `python3 todo.py complete <id>` marks a todo as completed
- Completed todos show `[done]` marker in list output
- Completing an already-complete todo prints a message (not an error)
- Invalid ID prints error message
- Completion state persists in todos.json

## Dependencies
- Requires demo-001.1.1 (add/list) to be complete first
- Builds on TodoApp class and JSON persistence

## Implementation Notes
- Add complete() method to TodoApp
- ID matching: prefix match (user can type first few chars)
- Update completed field to True and save

## Test Specifications

### Unit Tests (test_todo.py)
- test_complete_marks_todo_done
- test_complete_persists_state
- test_complete_invalid_id_raises
- test_complete_already_done_is_noop

### Manual Verification
- python3 todo.py add "Test" → note the ID
- python3 todo.py complete <id> → prints confirmation
- python3 todo.py list → shows [done] marker
- Restart and list → done state preserved

title: Consider SQLite storage for todos
description:
Evaluate SQLite as a storage backend instead of JSON file.

## Research Topics
- sqlite3 standard library module
- Schema design for todos table
- Migration path from JSON to SQLite
- Concurrent access considerations

## Why This is Parked
JSON file storage is sufficient for MVP. SQLite adds complexity without clear benefit for a single-user CLI tool.

## When to Revisit
- If we add search/filter functionality
- If data grows beyond what JSON handles well
- If we need concurrent access
